content:
I noticed that the definitions CategoryTheory.Abelian.instIsStableUnderCobaseChangeMonomorphisms and CategoryTheory.Abelian.instIsStableUnderBaseChangeEpimorphisms in Mathlib appear in two different files: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.CommSq and Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Monomorphisms.

Apparently, Lean accepts duplicate theorems (but no other type of definition) in different files. So if you have

-- File1.lean
theorem mythm {a : Nat} : a = a := rfl

-- File2.lean
theorem mythm (b : Nat) : b = b := rfl

Then this succeeds

import File1
import File2

#check mythm -- mythm (b : Nat) : b = b
#check mythm 37 -- mythm 37 : 37 = 37

but flipping the order of imports results in an error:

import File2
import File1

#check mythm -- mythm {a : Nat} : a = a
#check mythm 37 -- error

I think only binder types and names are permitted to switch, if the type signature differs between the files it will be invalid when you try to import both files at once.

Apparently this is an intentional feature and is documented here but I was wondering if maybe there was some way to mitigate this issue, like with a linter.
I remember this was discussed in some other thread I can't find, and it looked like something changed about autogenerated lemmas which meant this feature is no longer necessary. Not sure

One discussion was here #mathlib4 > Duplicate theorem: List.take_one_drop_eq_of_lt_length @ 💬 but I vaguely remember another one where at least one core developer weighed in (and indeed my memory was also that the conclusion was that this feature was no longer necessary).
